subject: Unit economics deep-dive / next steps (FintechX)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@fintechx.com>, Leah Wong <leah@fintechx.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Unit economics deep-dive / next steps (FintechX)

Thanks for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all stay aligned.

Call recap:
- Primary use case: real-time customer support + post-chat summarization for merchant onboarding.
- Expected adoption: pilot late Q3, production ramp into Q4.
- Initial volume estimate (customer guidance): 80–120M tokens / month once in production.

Key commercial asks from FintechX on today’s call:
- Target inference cost goal: ~ $/1M tokens (Samir mentioned wanting to get to a predictable $/1M metric for unit-econ planning).
- Budget range: initial pilot budget of ~$8k–$15k / month, scaling thereafter (open to committed tiers).
- CAC/payback: target 4–6 month payback for new acquisition flows tied to the feature.

What we’ll provide (next):
1) Unit-economics sensitivity model showing scenarios at 50/100/150M tokens/month (attached: unit_econ_model.xlsx).
2) Short slide summary of recommended pricing/commit tiers and expected $/feature impact (will share PDF).
3) A proposal for a Dedicated/Committed tier vs hosted pay-as-you-go with estimated monthly cost and break-even.

Asks from FintechX:
- Can you confirm which volume scenario feels most realistic (80 vs 100 vs 120M)?
- Do you have a hard budget ceiling for pilot month-to-month vs committed?
- Any specific latency SLOs or peak concurrency windows dev team should know about?

I’m attaching a working unit-econ model (Excel) we’ll use in the deep-dive; we can iterate on assumptions live. If this looks good I’ll loop in Solutions to book a 60-min deep-dive next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- unit_econ_model.xlsx (Excel workbook, 120 KB)

From: Samir Gupta <samir@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah Wong <leah@fintechx.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive / next steps (FintechX)

Thanks Marissa — quick clarifications from our side after reviewing the recap: 

1) Volume: pilot is likely closer to 60–80M tokens/month, but if conversion lifts as expected we should be at ~100M by month 3 of prod. Please include scenarios at 60/100/140M.
2) Budget: for pilot we can commit to $8k–$12k / month. If the Dedicated/commit options show real cost improvements we can negotiate a 6–12 month commit.
3) Target $/1M tokens: our finance team is modeling to $100–$150 / 1M tokens as acceptable for unit economics (this is net inference cost, pre-margin). If your model shows we land in that band with Dedicated + quantization, that’s promising.
4) CAC payback: yes, 4–6 months is what product leadership expects. They’ll want per-feature revenue assumptions baked into the model.

Would appreciate 2–3 sensitivity scenarios: conservative, base, upside, and a simple row showing expected gross margin at each scenario assuming feature-driven revenue of $0.10 per MAU action (we can provide exact revenue assumptions if helpful).

I'll stand by for the workbook and slides — can do a deep-dive on Tue/Wed next week.

—Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Product | FintechX
samir@fintechx.com

- Can we show both Hosted (pay-as-you-go) and Dedicated (6/12mo commit) pricing with expected $/1M after batching + KV caching + int8 quantization? Please include optimistic and conservative perf assumptions.

Deliverables: updated unit_econ_model.xlsx, one-page PDF summary dl-unit-econ-presentation.pdf, and a recommended commit level to hit $/1M = ~$125 (if possible).

I’ll propose Tue 2026-06-30 10:00 AM PT for a 60-min deep-dive with FintechX — can you confirm availability?

Thanks — Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive / next steps (FintechX)

Samir — thanks for the quick clarification. Attached is a short PDF summary and an updated Excel model with the three requested scenarios (60 / 100 / 140M tokens). Highlights up front: 

- Base scenario (100M tokens): Hosted (pay-as-you-go) estimate: $/1M = ~$220; Dedicated (6-mo commit with batching + int8 quant) estimate: $/1M = ~$120.
- Conservative (60M): Dedicated benefit is smaller; $/1M ~= $170 vs $280 hosted.
- Upside (140M): Dedicated stretch: $/1M ~= $95.

Per-feature and CAC calculations (summary):
- Example: If feature drives 250k MAU actions / month and revenue per action = $0.10, monthly feature revenue = $25k. At base scenario with $/1M = $120 (100M tokens ~ 12 * $/1M units) inference cost ~ $1,440 (this is illustrative — see sheet).
- CAC payback: with current cost to acquire a customer at $150 and incremental ARPA assumptions in the workbook, payback windows range 3.5–6 months across scenarios.
- Margin targets: to maintain >60% gross margin we need inference cost to be <= ~15% of feature revenue; base scenario meets this with Dedicated commit.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached workbook and slides: dl-unit-econ-presentation.pdf + unit_econ_model.xlsx (both attached as stubs).
2) Confirm availability for Tue 2026-06-30 10:00 AM PT for the deep-dive (I’ll send a calendar invite once confirmed).
3) If you want us to produce a formal pricing proposal for a 6- or 12-month commit we can include exact commit discounts and SLA language.

> On Fri, Jun 26, 2026 at 09:11 AM Samir Gupta <samir@fintechx.com> wrote:

> > Budget: for pilot we can commit to $8k–$12k / month.
> > Target $/1M tokens: our finance team is modeling to $100–$150 / 1M tokens as acceptable for unit economics.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.
